set.beta: Burnt Boot Peak (P 6480) sits across the Middle Fork of the Snoqualmie River, about two miles southeast of Big Snow Mountain. From the base of the steepest part of the north ridge, three leads of fifth class on granite, the last along a very sharp crest, reach easier ground; three more leads of class 3 and 4 gain the summit. The peak's first ascent, by a 1963 survey party, came by an easier scramble line. No repeat ascents of the ridge are recorded, so expect little to no modern traffic.

review.changed: beta quoted the first-ascent note word for word and named its author; rewritten in plain voice with the same facts (no-sources rule). fa unchanged.

set.overview: A rarely repeated, sustained alpine ice line up a series of runnels and couloirs just right of the true summit on Summit Chief's north side, with unusually continuous ice climbing for a Cascade route.

review.changed: overview credited a named climber's opinion; restated as a plain description (no-sources rule). fa unchanged.
